title: Resilience Ops Digest — incidents, SLO review, and on-call handoffs (Apr 19–25, 2026)
content:
Summary:
This week (Apr 19–25) focused on two medium-severity incidents, an SLO drift for the embeddings service during the spike on Apr 21, and a smoother-than-expected on-call rotation transition on Apr 24. This digest captures timelines, quick mitigations, SLO telemetry, handoff notes, and concrete follow-ups for the next sprint.

Highlights:
- Incident A: 2026-04-21 13:02 UTC — transient latency spike for embeddings-v1 used by search pipeline (SLA impact window ~18m).
- Incident B: 2026-04-23 02:47 UTC — autoscaler misconfiguration caused a brief scaling loop for dedicated GPU pool (12m elevated error rate for dedicated customers).
- SLO Review: embeddings service p99 latency violated 0.5% budget on Apr 21; root cause related to sudden request-size distribution shift and suboptimal batching.
- Handoff: On-call rotation (week of Apr 18–24) completed; documented lessons and updated the runbook for embedding-size heuristics.

Incidents (detailed):
1) Embeddings latency spike (Incident A)
- Detection: Alert SRE-EMB-LAT-CRIT fired at 2026-04-21 13:03 UTC (alert threshold: p99 > 400ms). First pager to on-call at 13:04.
- Impact: p99 latency rose to ~920ms for ~18 minutes; error rate unchanged. Affects hosted/search pipeline customers with large-batch requests.
- Timeline (key events):
  - 13:02:10 UTC — spike begins (observed in traces and aggregated metrics).
  - 13:04 UTC — on-call paged (Carlos).
  - 13:06 UTC — temporary mitigation: force-smaller-batch policy applied via feature flag (zara/ff-force-small-batches).
  - 13:10 UTC — p99 begins to decline; by 13:20 back to normal.
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden influx of long-context batched inference requests that exceeded the typical sequence-length distribution, causing kernel choice to pick a slower path and increasing KV cache pressure.
- Immediate fixes:
  - Reverted to conservative batching for requests > 10k tokens (FF enabled).
  - Increased short-term concurrency cap for embeddings workers to avoid queuing hotspots.
- Follow-ups (owners):
  - (Anika) Add preflight request-size histogram to the routing tier to reject/route very large batches to a fallback queue (due 2026-05-05).
  - (Ethan) Investigate kernel-selection telemetry and add metric for 'slow-kernel' decisions (due 2026-05-01).
  - (Priya) Draft changelog note and customer comms for affected customers (due 2026-04-27).

2) Dedicated pool autoscaler loop (Incident B)
- Detection: Elevated errors from dedicated jobs starting 02:47 UTC; automated alert SRE-AUTO-ERR triggered.
- Impact: ~12 minutes of increased 5xx responses for scheduled dedicated inference jobs in eu-west region; immediate customer-facing timeouts for queued jobs.
- Timeline:
  - 02:47 UTC — first errors.
  - 02:50 UTC — SRE on-call (Zara) traces reveal a misapplied HPA patch in release-engineering->autoscaler config (PR 987 merged 02:30 UTC).
  - 02:55 UTC — roll back PR to previous autoscaler configuration; error rate drops by 03:00 UTC.
- Root cause: config drift introduced an aggressive cooldown on scale-down leading to frequent up/down cycles under bursty load.
- Immediate action: rollback and tighten pre-merge autoscaler integration tests.
- Follow-ups (owners) :
  - (Ethan) Expand autoscaler canary tests in release pipeline to include sustained-burst scenario (due 2026-05-10).
  - (Carlos) Add a CI gating step that simulates queue pressure for PRs touching /autoscaler (due 2026-05-04).

SLO telemetry and interpretation:
- SLOs checked this week: embeddings-p99-latency (SLO target: 99.5th percentile < 400ms monthly), hosted-api-availability (target: 99.9%).
- Week summary: hosted-api availability held at 99.995% for the week. Embeddings p99 breached on Apr 21 for a 24-hour window equivalent of ~0.7% monthly error budget burn (short-term).
- Notes: The burst shows a pattern where few large batch requests can disproportionately consume p99 budget. We recommend adding a soft quota for max batch token size per tenant and a weighted batching policy.

On-call handoff notes (rotation Apr 18–24 -> Apr 25–May 01):
- Outgoing on-call: Carlos Rivera
  - Reminder: embeddings runbook v2.1 has the new 'force small batches' feature flag and the fallback queue instructions.
  - Ongoing actions: follow-ups for Incident A (owns customer comms).
- Incoming on-call: Nisha Verma
  - Recommended reading before first pager: runbook sections "embeddings-sizing", "autoscaler-troubleshooting", and the newest SLO dashboard links.
  - Contact points: Priya Nair (escalation), Anika Patel (autoscaler lead), Ethan Brooks (kernel/runtime).
- Handoff checklist completed: runbooks verified, Slack channel pinned messages updated, escalation contact matrix confirmed.

Runbook and tooling changes this week:
- Added 'request-size histogram' probe to the routing tier for early detection (prototype in feature branch, see linked PR).
- Updated embeddings runbook with step-by-step FF toggles and metrics to observe when toggling (section added v2.1).
- Autoscaler CI gating ticket opened (SRE-4321) to require integration test pass for PRs modifying autoscaler config.

Action items (priority ordered):
1) Add token-size soft quotas and tenant-level reject/route behavior (owner: Anika, eta 2026-05-05).
2) Kernel decision telemetry and alert (owner: Ethan, eta 2026-05-01).
3) Autoscaler sustained-burst test in CI (owner: Ethan, eta 2026-05-10).
4) Customer comms draft for affected hosted customers (owner: Priya, eta 2026-04-27).
5) Runbook tabletop exercise for on-call covering combined embedding+autoscaler failure mode (owner: Carlos, schedule: week of 2026-05-03).

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we automatically deny/soft-queue requests that exceed a new token threshold, or route them to a paid "large-batch" tier? (cost vs user experience tradeoff)
- How aggressive should 'slow-kernel' fallback be? Add hysteresis or require multiple samples?
- Metrics: do we need a new cardinality-reduced label for batch-size buckets to keep time-series costs low?

Notes to self / quick hits:
- Observed that the embeddings spike coincided with a partner data-export job; follow-up with Solutions Eng to identify tenant (tracking in SRE-4324).
- Keep a one-line summary for customer comms: "Short latency spike on Apr 21 caused by unusually large batched requests; we applied mitigations and are rolling permanent protections."

Appendix — short logs and helpful links:
- Alert ids: SRE-EMB-LAT-CRIT-20260421, SRE-AUTO-ERR-20260423
- PRs referenced: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987
- Tickets: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4321, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4324
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Runbook+Index

If you're reviewing this: please skim the action items and reply with any objections to owners/etas by EOD Tuesday 2026-04-28. We'll lock follow-up tasks into the SRE sprint planning meeting on 2026-04-29.

-- Priya
SRE (oncall coordinator)
